prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on the complexity of your case, whether you need extractions/bone grafts, your budget/insurance, and your comfort with the clinician. I can help you find a great provider; here’s how to identify one and what to ask.

What to look for
- Specialty training: for implants, look for an oral and maxillofacial surgeon, a periodontist, or a prosthodontist who focuses on implants. These specialists have advanced training beyond general dentistry.
- Board certification or fellowship: e.g., ABOMS (oral surgeons), AAID credentials, or prosthodontist certification through the American College of Prosthodontists.
- Experience: number of implants placed per year and experience with cases similar to yours (single tooth, full-arch, immediate load).
- Technology: CBCT 3D imaging, guided surgery, digital prosthetics/scan, and in-office lab relationships.
- Coordination of care: close collaboration between surgeon and restorative dentist (prosthodontist) for predictable esthetic and functional results.
- Before/after photos and patient references; consistently good reviews on multiple platforms (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp).
- Clear treatment plan, timeline, costs, and warranty/aftercare policy.

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants have you placed? How many similar to my case?
- Are you a specialist? Board certifications?
- Do you use 3D imaging and guided surgery?
- Who will make and place the final crown/bridge — you or a restorative dentist?
- What are the risks, alternatives, expected timeline, and total cost (including all phases)?
- Do you offer sedation or IV anesthesia if I’m anxious?
- Can you show before/after photos and share patient references?

How to verify and where to search
- Check ABOMS, AAID, AAP, or ACP directories for credential verification.
- Read multiple review sites and look for consistency.
- Check Colorado Dental Board for disciplinary history.

Would you like me to find highly rated implant specialists in Denver and give you a short list with contact details and ratings? If so, tell me whether you prefer a specialist type (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist), whether you have dental insurance, and whether you need complex work (bone grafts, extractions, full-arch).
